query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

message.content:
Below you’ll find two ways to spin‑up a **Google Cloud** virtual machine that has:

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| Image | `ubuntu-os-cloud` → *Ubuntu 20.04 LTS* (`2004-focal`) |
| Machine type | Any “high‑CPU” family – e.g. `e2-standard-8` (8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM) |
| Accelerator | One **NVIDIA® RTX A6000** (GPU) |
| Zone | Pick one that supports GPUs (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `asia-east1-b`). |

> ⚠️ Make sure:
>
> - Your project has **Compute Engine API** enabled.
> - Billing is attached.
> - You have the necessary IAM permissions (`roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1`).
> - The zone you pick actually offers the `nvidia-tesla-a100`‑like accelerators; if not, adjust to another supported GPU (the closest match at present is `nvidia-tesla-v100`).

---

### Option 1 – Using the `gcloud` CLI  

```bash
# Set variables first
PROJECT="my-gcp-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-radeon-instance \
    --project=${PROJECT} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=e2-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM
    --subnet=default \
    --network-tier=PREMIUM \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --provisioning-model=BASIC \
    --service-account=my-sa@${PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --metadata=startup-script='#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470' \
    --create-disk=size=50,type=pd-balanced,image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts,image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a100   # <-- replace with actual GPU type available
```

> **Note:**  
> At the moment Google Cloud does not expose an official `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
> The nearest equivalent is `nvidia-tesla-a100`; if your workload specifically demands an RTX A6000, consider using a custom AMI via [GKE](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/gpu-support) or waiting until the hardware becomes available.

If you do eventually see `nvidia-tesla-a6000` listed under `--accelerator-types list`, just swap out the type above.

---

### Option 2 – Direct REST API Call (curl)

This uses the Compute Engine **instances.insert** endpoint. Replace placeholders appropriately.

```bash
# Variables
API_ENDPOINT="https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT}/zones/${ZONE}"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)
INSTANCE_NAME="my-radeon-instance"

cat <<EOF > payload.json
{
  "name": "${INSTANCE_NAME}",
  "machineType": "projects/${PROJECT}/zones/${ZONE}/machineTypes/e2-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "labels": { },
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network":"global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs":[{"type":"ONE_TO_ONE_NAT","name":"External NAT"}]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/${PROJECT}/zones/${ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ]
}
EOF

curl -X POST "$API_ENDPOINT/insert" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d @payload.json
```

#### What each field means

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance hostname |
| `machineType` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `disks[0].initializeParams.sourceImage` | Base OS image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS) |
| `networkInterfaces[*]` | Default VPC + external IP |
| `guestAccelerators[*]` | Attach GPU(s); change `acceleratorType` if a different GPU is required |
| `scheduling.onHostMaintenance` | Keep running during host maintenance events |

After sending the request, you'll receive an Operation resource. Poll `/operations/{operationId}` until `"status":"DONE"` to confirm creation succeeded.

---

### Quick sanity check after launch

Once the VM boots, SSH into it and verify drivers & CUDA:

```bash
ssh USERNAME@EXTERNAL_IP
nvidia-smi            # Should show RTX A6000 (or whatever GPU was provisioned)
nvcc --version         # Verify CUDA toolkit installed
```

That’s all! Adjust the machine type, disk size, or network settings per your specific requirements. Happy computing!
